conclusion: The provisioned STATS_NZ_API_KEY authenticates against two live Stats NZ surfaces and is decisively NOT a Koordinates API token. (1) Aotearoa Data Explorer SDMX: unauthenticated data requests return HTTP 401, keyed requests return HTTP 200 CSV; the public catalogue lists 913 dataflows including 335 CEN23 tables. (2) Stats NZ Geographic Data Service (datafinder): the layer catalogue, per-layer/version metadata and per-layer attachments are public, so 20 objects covering the six electorate boundary layers were captured byte-for-byte into CAS and sha256-verified (attribute CSVs for 2025/2020 general and Maori electorates, PDFs, plus metadata for all six). The same key is rejected by the datafinder spatial-query and data-table services (HTTP 403 invalid-api-key), which require a Koordinates token with the query scope, and the geometry export API returns HTTP 401 without one. The WFS gateway accepts the key but exposes no FeatureType entries, so no geometry bytes were captured. The legacy OData host api.stats.govt.nz is still unusable (expired certificate plus HTTP 502 even with TLS verification bypassed). Boundary GEOMETRY re-capture therefore remains blocked on a Koordinates account/token; boundary ATTRIBUTE data is now captured.
next_actions: Stop targeting api.stats.govt.nz/opendata/v1; Stats NZ now names datafinder.stats.govt.nz as its primary geospatial service.
Obtain a Koordinates ID (free) and an API token with the query/download scope for datafinder geometry export; the Stats NZ subscription key is confirmed not to be a Koordinates token.
After export, capture GeoJSON/SHP for layers 122741, 122742, 104580, 104579, 104062, 104065 into CAS with per-file receipts and merge with the attribute capture.
Keep STATS_NZ_API_KEY in the repo-local .env (gitignored) or a CI secret; never commit it. Store any Koordinates token the same way.
ADE CEN23 tables are a separate rights-reviewed follow-up; the catalogue and one keyed slice are proven reproducible here.
